scope: Independent visual observations of the six bound images only. This records images actually viewed in the preceding review; this record-writing step did not rerender, reopen images, calculate raw geometry, or issue model/photographic-accuracy acceptance.
conclusion: No major omitted architectural feature, mirrored arrangement or reversed high/low massing could be clearly established from these six views. This is limited negative evidence, not a complete-shape or photographic-precision PASS.

visible_feature_observations.observation: The full native view shows the high mass and lower wing, consistent with the supplied high-north/low-south orientation context, together with continuous stepped yellow bands and vertically divided curtain-wall layers. The main museum composition remains recognizable.

The detail native view shows a silver curved shell, narrow vertical glazed slots, curved curtain-wall grids and horizontal shading elements. These are actual visible modeled elements; their complete measured dimensions are not verified by this comparison.
The rear native view shows the rounded taller mass, descending lower mass, layered yellow bands and a yellow zigzag external stair. The stair is visibly present.

visual_differences_retained.observation: The photographs have a much stronger cantilever and deeply recessed shadow beneath the upper C-shaped shell. In the native full view the relationship reads flatter and the silver edge appears thinner.
visual_differences_retained.interpretation: This is a perceived visual difference in the supplied views. Without calibrated matching cameras and lighting it does not establish a specific geometry error or a missing cantilever.

visual_differences_retained.observation: The external stair reads visually finer/thinner in the native rear view than in the reference photograph.
visual_differences_retained.interpretation: The viewpoints and projection types differ, so apparent width alone is insufficient to establish a dimensional or missing-part defect.

limitations: The photograph cameras were not calibrated or matched to the renderer. Root identified full as a1.7m/45mm perspective view and detail/rear as orthographic; these are supplied context, not camera parameters independently measured in this visual review.
Neutral rendering illumination, photographic daylight/twilight, reflection, exposure and environment differ. Shading or apparent edge thickness was not treated by itself as a geometry error.

The three reference photos do not clearly expose the same entire slotted shell surface shown in the detail render. Full slot count, interval, width and depth cannot be verified from this six-image comparison.
North/south naming follows the already supplied source orientation context; the images alone do not constitute a geographic orientation measurement.

Only visible external surfaces in these images were compared. Hidden sides, interior, full exterior dimensional accuracy, material optical accuracy, all viewpoints, model contact/collision and actual browser behavior were not assessed.
No PASS for photographic precision or complete external shape is issued. Existing root native acceptance and independent geometry reports retain their own distinct scopes.
